_readme: TWO CATALOGUES, and the split is the whole design.
upgrades[] — IN-LEVEL TALENTS. Drafted during a run, gone when it ends.
home[]     — PERMANENT UPGRADES. Bought at home with ⭐, kept forever.
THE LINE BETWEEN THEM: a talent changes WHAT YOU KNOW about the house in
front of you; a home upgrade changes HOW YOU PLAY. Only the second is safe
to make permanent. Sixth Sense tells you where a held item lives — carrying
that between levels would gut the taxonomy the game is about, and 4-2 was
already being played with it in hand back when talents did carry over. So
the information talents stay per-run and the friction ones went home.
WHAT CHANGED, so it does not get changed back:
⭐ IS A WALLET NOW. It used to be lifetime score that was never spent, and
this file used to carry a costs[] array that was deleted because nothing
read it. Prices are read. `cost` on a home upgrade is per LEVEL taken, and
`cost` on a client in clients.json is a one-off unlock. Do not delete them
again on the grounds that stars are score — they are money.
draftSteps IS GONE. Drafts used to be granted by crossing lifetime-⭐
thresholds [4,10,18,28,40,55,72], which gave a LEVEL no say in how many
rewards it handed out — the count fell out of how many rows it happened to
contain. The first threshold was crossed on the last item of 1-2, which is
why every level before 5-1 carried "talents": false: a workaround for
having no per-level control. A level now authors `rewards: N` and grants a
pick on each of its first N ROOM completions, and the workaround is gone.
hands LEFT THIS LIST for home[]. That took the in-level pool down to four
talents and seven picks, which a five-pick house drains — so keyring,
label and skeleton were written to refill it. Seven talents, twelve picks.
levels — how many times a thing can be taken. That is the whole knob.
desc supports {token} and {token|sec} (milliseconds -> seconds), resolved
against that entry's params. An unresolvable token is a boot error.
EVERY id HERE MUST BE IMPLEMENTED. TALENT_IDS and STORE_IDS in js/config.js
are the lists the code actually reads, and boot validation compares them
against this file IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Adding an entry here and nowhere else
used to give you a card that animated, said its name, incremented a level
and did nothing whatsoever — invisible, because a talent that does nothing
looks exactly like a talent you misunderstood. A home upgrade in that state
would also take the player's money.
WHAT WAS CUT, AND WHY, so it doesn't get reinvented:
Magnet Fingers used to fire on PICK-UP: grabbing an item also grabbed
matching items within 14% of the room. Measured over 180 generated rooms
and 10,272 floor items, that condition was true 8.1% of the time — a
talent that did nothing in 92 pick-ups out of 100. The fantasy was right
and the moment was wrong: duplicates exist (71.7% of items have one loose
in the same room) but they are scattered, so requiring them to be NEAR
each other threw the talent away. It now fires on PUT-AWAY, where being
near each other doesn't matter.
Tidy Whirlwind sorted the items already inside containers into clean rows.
It filed nothing off the floor, so it never moved the only number the
player is watching. It also cost a HUD button, a cooldown ticker, a
once-a-second interval and a consumable to refresh it.
_picksNote: WHEN A HOUSE TEACHES A TALENT, and how many.
It used to be ROOM completions: a level authored `rewards: N` and got a pick
on each of its first N rooms. That was too late, and worst exactly where it
hurt most — a small house finishes its first room most of the way through
itself, so the talent arrived with nothing left to use it on. And 11 of the
34 campaign levels authored 0, so the first talent a new player ever saw was
on the TWELFTH level.
Now it is ROWS, and the numbers are DERIVED from the size of the house that
actually generated rather than authored per level. A row is the same unit the
⭐ economy already counts, it fires often enough to place a pick anywhere in a
run, and deriving means the 215 procedural free-play houses are covered by
the same rule with nothing to author.
tiers — how many picks, by the house's total row count. Read in order; the
first `upTo` the house does not exceed wins. `upTo: null` is the
last one and catches everything above.
at    — WHERE in the house each pick lands, as fractions of total rows,
indexed by how many picks there are. FRONT-LOADED on purpose: the
first should arrive while there is still a house to use it on, and
the last stops well short of the end so it never lands on top of
the client's outro and the win screen. Nothing fires at 100%.
A level may still author `rewards: N` to override its tier — for a house that
should defy its size. Nothing in the campaign does today.
TWO CARDS, NOT THREE. `draftCards` was 3, which with a small pool meant every
draft was a survey of nearly everything rather than a decision. Two makes the
choice real and is meant to be played against a pool that is deliberately
small and well understood.

upgrades._note: INTUITION IS A LADDER, and it used to be one card. `sense` told you the room AND the container the moment you took it, and `homesick` was the glow on its own — so between them the taxonomy the game is about was answered in one pick, with nowhere left to scale. Split into the three rungs it always had: it glows, then it names the room, then it names the container.
upgrades.name: Intuition
upgrades.desc: Level 1: anything on this floor that lives in this room glows. Level 2: what you're holding tells you which room. Level 3: and which piece of furniture.

upgrades._note: MAGNET FINGERS AND ONE TRIP WERE THE SAME TALENT. One helped from the floor, one from your hands, they sat in the same function, and drafting either felt like nothing happened — because each moved one or two items, silently, inside an action you were already performing. Merged, and the levels are meant to be felt: give it real magnitude and its own sound, or it will read as nothing again.
upgrades.name: Tidy Hands
upgrades.desc: Putting something away takes {pull} more of its kind with it — from your hands and off this floor. Level 2 sends anything in your hands that lives there too. More per level.

upgrades.name: Label Maker
upgrades.desc: Furniture owns up to {show} thing it is still completely missing. One more per level.

_storeNote: HOME. Bought with ⭐ at the main menu, kept forever, and the reason to keep
playing past the room in front of you.
cost   — ⭐ per level taken. An ARRAY prices each level separately (Bigger
Hands gets steeper); a NUMBER prices every level the same.
levels — how many times it can be bought.
PRICED AGAINST THE CAMPAIGN, not against free play, because free play mints
no stars at all (see the note in sizes.json). The 34 campaign levels pay
roughly 1 ⭐ per completed row, so a first run through the whole campaign is
in the low hundreds — enough to unlock most of the cast OR max two or three
upgrades, not both. Choosing is the point; replaying is the way out of a
`picks` IS THE ONE THAT FEEDS BACK INTO THE OTHER CATALOGUE: it raises how
many in-level talents a house hands out, on top of whatever the level
authored. It is capped by the level's own room count either way — a house
cannot grant a pick for a room it does not have.

store._note: THE ONE THING IN THE STORE, and priced to be the long chase. The complaint was never the size of the effect — it was that the intro alone paid for three extra slots. It is the most powerful and most wanted upgrade in the game, so maxing it is now most of everything a whole campaign pays (120 of ~136 ⭐). Same four levels, five slots to nine.
store.name: Bigger Hands
store.desc: +1 hand slot, in every house, forever. Haul more per trip.

_consumableNote: One-offs, used to back-fill a draft when there aren't `draftCards` talents
left to offer. `effect` must be in CONSUMABLE_EFFECTS (js/config.js).
CURRENTLY UNREACHABLE, and that is fine. A house grants at most three picks
and the talent pool is deeper than three levels, so the back-fill has nothing
to do until the pool shrinks or a house teaches far more. Kept because the
path is written and tested and the next pool change could need it.
THREE HAVE BEEN DELETED FOR THE SAME REASON, and it is the reason to be
suspicious of anything in this list. Second Wind and X-Ray Eyes set a field
on the run that NOTHING EVER READ — drafted, animated, named, no effect.
Lucky Find paid +3 ⭐ that never reached the wallet, because this module
cannot see js/store.js and nobody noticed the missing addStars() for as long
as it existed. X-Ray's idea was worth keeping and became a real talent (the
glow that is now Intuition rung 1); the other two were noise.

consumables.name: Drop Everything
consumables.desc: Right now: everything in your hands that lives in this room goes home.
